primary: ML researchers from NLP, RL, computer vision, or general deep learning who work with or are curious about LLM-based systems but do not specialize in AI agents or software engineering automation
secondary: Systems researchers interested in infrastructure for AI evaluation; ML practitioners evaluating agent frameworks
assumed_knowledge: Large language models (LLMs) and transformer architectures
Standard ML evaluation methodology (train/val/test splits, benchmarks, metrics)
Basic software engineering concepts (code execution, APIs, command line)
Reinforcement learning basics (agents, environments, actions, observations)
Docker containers at a conceptual level
Common ML benchmarks (e.g., ImageNet, GLUE) as reference for how benchmarks work
term_budget: define all subfield-specific terms on first use
binding_personas: NLP researcher familiar with LLM prompting but not agent infrastructure
RL researcher who thinks of agents in terms of Gym-style environments
ML practitioner evaluating whether to use OpenHands for their own agent research
